South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 05/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and evaluation of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit, primarily to evaluate his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management, persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and ongoing fatigue. He reports that his dyspnea has not significantly improved despite continued use of his inhaler regimen. He continues to utilize the albuterol inhaler up to eight times daily, particularly during increased physical activity and in response to recent weather changes, which he believes have exacerbated his symptoms.
The bilateral lower extremity edema persists, and Mr. Fairfax notes that he has been compliant with dietary sodium restrictions and continues to take furosemide at 80 mg daily. However, he reports no significant change in the edema, which remains 1+ pitting and is more pronounced after prolonged sitting. He denies any associated pain, warmth, or erythema.
Mr. Fairfax expresses ongoing fatigue that continues to limit his engagement in social activities and his ability to perform daily tasks. He also reports a slight worsening of his psychological symptoms, including increased anxiety and depressive episodes, which he attributes to his chronic health conditions and the challenges posed by limited mobility.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, increased use to eight times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily. 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 84, BP 128/78, RR 28, O2 sat 85% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.5, Hgb 11.1, Hct 33.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.1, Cl 95, CO2 23, BUN 24, Cr 1.5, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 520 (slight increase). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: The patient continues to experience significant dyspnea despite ongoing therapy. Given the increased use of the albuterol inhaler, a review of his inhaler technique will be conducted. A referral to a pulmonary rehabilitation program is recommended to enhance his functional capacity and address his respiratory symptoms. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists and has not improved. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs. A nephrology referral will be arranged for further evaluation if no improvement is observed in the next follow-up. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Given the ongoing symptoms of fatigue and exacerbated anxiety/depression, continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Schedule follow-up with a psychologist for ongoing support. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
